# A dialog that was moved can no longer be resized

## Context

Reported inside #21271 ("Framework resize integration") by @armando-ota, whose own desktop needed an adapter to keep resized dialogs at their new size. Reproduced on `dev` at `a2d97b19b8` in `examples/dialog`, in a real browser with pointer gestures on the right resize handle (+150 px):

| Run | Width before | Width after release | Preview width mid-gesture |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fresh dialog, not moved | 410 px | 557 px | 409.594 px (start size) |
| Same dialog after one header move | 410 px | 410 px | 409.594 px (start size) |

## The Problem

A resizable dialog stops resizing after its first move, which is the most common sequence for a window: the handles show, the cursor changes, the gesture runs, and nothing changes. Before the first move a resize lands, but its preview never follows the pointer: the dialog fades to 0.3 and jumps to the new size on release. Every `dialog.Base` with `resizable: true` is affected, including the web desktop's app windows (#21198).

## The Architectural Reality

- Design authority: the dialog's `@member {Boolean} resizable_=true` (`src/dialog/Base.mjs:131`). A gesture on handles the dialog renders, that changes nothing, is a defect rather than a policy.
- A move writes its geometry into the dialog's `style` config: `dialog.Base#onDragEnd` (`src/dialog/Base.mjs:672-714`) sets `height`, `left`, `top` and `width` in px, plus `opacity: 1` and `transform: 'none'`.
- A resize writes into the owner's `wrapperStyle`: `Resizable#onDragStart` sets `opacity: 0.3` (`src/plugin/Resizable.mjs:386-401`), `Resizable#onDragEnd` copies the proxy's geometry (`src/plugin/Resizable.mjs:279-300`, marked `// todo: delegation target`).
- `component.Base#updateStyle` (`src/component/Base.mjs:2091-2100`) renders a single-root component (`vdom === vdomRoot`, as a dialog is) with `{...wrapperStyle, ...style}`: every key in `style` masks the same key in `wrapperStyle`. After a move, `style` holds `width`, `height` and `opacity`, so both the resized size and the 0.3 fade are masked.
- The preview fails the same way: `DragZone` sizes the proxy in its `style` (`src/draggable/DragZone.mjs:388-395`), and `Resizable#onDragMove` writes the proxy's `wrapperStyle` (`src/plugin/Resizable.mjs:309-382`). On release, the `wrapperStyle` getter (`src/component/Base.mjs:1202-1203`) lets the written value win, which is why an unmoved dialog still lands at the right size.
- The animated show writes its geometry straight to the DOM through `Neo.applyDeltas` (`src/dialog/Base.mjs:466-477`), into neither config. That is why a fresh dialog has no masking `style.width`. `animateShow` (`src/dialog/Base.mjs:420`) reads `style` (`style?.height`, `style?.left`, ...) as the size and position to reopen at, so a moved dialog reopens where the user left it.

## The Fix

Decided at intake (2026-11-17), revised during implementation: move and resize write gesture geometry through one channel, so the later gesture wins.

- `Neo.plugin.Resizable` gets `styleConfig`, the style config that takes the resize on its owner and on its drag proxy, defaulting to `'wrapperStyle'`. `dialog.Base` passes `'style'`, where its moves (`onDragEnd`) and its reopen (`animateShow`) already keep the geometry. The drag proxy is sized in `style` by `DragZone`, so the preview follows too.
- The grid and table header plugins call `super.onDragStart`, `super.onDragMove` and `super.onDragEnd` (`src/grid/header/plugin/Resizable.mjs:54,110,149`, `src/table/header/plugin/Resizable.mjs:61,96,141`) and keep the default, so column resizing does not change. `src/board/CardEditor.mjs` and `src/timeline/EventEditor.mjs` set `resizable: false`.
- Revised away from moving `dialog.Base#onDragEnd` to `wrapperStyle`: a dialog created with `style: {left, top}`, as `examples/dialog`'s second dialog is, keeps those keys in `style` through `animateShow`. They would mask every move written to `wrapperStyle`.

Prescription checked: `src/plugin/Resizable.mjs` — owns the concern (the channel it writes); `src/dialog/Base.mjs` names the channel its geometry lives in.

## Contract Ledger

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Neo.plugin.Resizable#styleConfig` (new, `'style'` or `'wrapperStyle'`) | this ticket | The style config the resize writes into, on the owner and on its drag proxy | `'wrapperStyle'`, the channel written on `dev`, so existing subclasses and owners are unchanged | JSDoc | e2e + unit |
| `Neo.dialog.Base`'s Resizable plugin | this ticket | Created with `styleConfig: 'style'`, the config its moves and reopen use; `resizablePluginConfig` can still override it | — | inline comment | e2e |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: A dialog moved by its header and then resized by a handle renders the resized size. A resize followed by a move keeps that size.
- [ ] AC-2: During a resize, the preview's size follows the pointer.
- [ ] AC-3: A moved dialog that is hidden and shown again with animation reopens at its moved position and size, as on `dev` today.
- [ ] AC-4: An e2e spec on `examples/dialog` pins AC-1 and AC-2 with real pointer gestures, each arm failing on `dev`. A unit spec cannot: the move reads the drag proxy's rect from the main thread.
- [ ] AC-5: Grid and table column resizing behaves as on `dev`: their header resize specs give the same results.

## Out of Scope

- Keeping dialogs inside a boundary container that shrinks: #21271.
- The window controls of desktop app windows: #21201.

Resizable dims its owner through the style config that takes the

wins the root style merge. Escape ends the gesture through the drag
zone's cancel, which removes the proxy and swallows the later drag:end,
so nothing undimmed the dialog. The plugin now records the owner's
opacity at drag:start and restores it at both ends: a release commits
the proxy's box, a cancel commits nothing. A release no longer forces
opacity 1 over a configured one."
